The '''1985-86 Division 1 season''' was the 48th since its establishment. [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] became champions for the first time in their history with 56 points. During this season the "Boulogne Boys" and "Gavroche" emerged. They were groups of supporters located in the [[Kop of Boulogne]] a stand in the [[Parc des Princes]]. On 26 July 1985, Paris Saint-Germain took the top spot in the league for the first time in their history after defeating [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] 3-1. On 20 September, ''Les Parisiens'' recovered from a 2-0 score and claimed a 2-3 victory over [[RC Lens|Lens]]. A victory that proved the strength of the current championship leader. On 29 November, Paris recorded a goalless draw against [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Girondins de Bordeaux]], setting a new record of 22 matches without defeat along the way (previously held by [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] in the [[French football Division 1 1957–58|1957-58]] season). The capital club would eventually lose against [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in the 20th matchday after recording a run of 27 matches without a single defeat. On 11 April 1986, [[Oumar Sène]] gave PSG the victory over [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco]] in stoppage time. Thanks to the victory, the club captained by [[Luis Fernández]] was virtually champion of [[France]], with four points ahead of the second and with a better goal difference. The club would become the first club from [[Paris]] to win the league since 1936. On 18 April, PSG lost 3-1 against [[FC Metz|Metz]] with a surprising ending that saw Paris goalkeeper [[Joël Bats]] abandon the pitch injured, leaving his place to Luis Fernández. On 25 April, Paris SG claimed their first league title after easily defeating [[SC Bastia|Bastia]] 3-1 at the Parc des Princes. After the match, fireworks blazed in the sky celebrating the first championship of the club. On 28 April, the Mayor of Paris, [[Jacques Chirac]], received the champion of France at the [[Hôtel de Ville, Paris|Paris City Hall]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://psg70.free.fr/accueil.htm | title=Saison 1985/86 | work=PSG70 | access-date=28 March 2010 }}</ref>
